chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, that he was asked about a man who prayed without taharah, or forgot prayers and did not perform them, or slept through them, so he said:

He should make it up when he remembers it, at whatever hour he remembers it, by night or by day. If the time of a salat enters and he has not completed what he had missed, then he should make up so long as he does not fear that the time of this present salat will pass; and this one has more right to its time, so he should perform it. Then when he has completed it, he should perform what he had missed from what has passed, and he should not perform even a single rak'ah of supererogatory prayer until he has completed making up the entire obligatory prayer.

key_terms.أَحَقُّ بِوَقْتِهَا: more entitled to its proper time, referring to the present prayer
key_terms.ذَكَرَهَا: he remembered it, referring to the missed prayer
key_terms.فَاتَهُ: what he missed of the obligatory prayers
key_terms.وَقْتُ صَلَاةٍ: the appointed time of a salat
key_terms.يَتَطَوَّعْ: to perform a voluntary or supererogatory prayer
key_terms.يَقْضِيهَا: he makes it up, meaning he performs the missed obligatory prayer

ai.seo_question: When making up missed salat, may a person perform voluntary prayers before completing the missed obligatory prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that missed obligatory prayers must be made up as soon as one remembers them, whether during the night or the day. However, when the time of a current salat enters, that present prayer takes priority if there is fear that its time may expire, and supererogatory prayer should be left until all missed obligatory prayers are completed.
